articles.title: Spotify is letting artists manually approve releases to combat AI fakes
articles.summary: Spotify’s Artist Profile Protection lets artists manually approve what music shows up on their profile.
articles.body: Spotify is beta-testing a new feature called Artist Profile Protection that lets artists review releases before they go live. Sometimes songs end up on the wrong artist pages because of metadata mixups or shared names. But increasingly, artists have been targeted by impostors and AI-generated fakes. Profile Protection offers a buffer against bad actors. Everyone from Drake and Beyoncé, to experimental composers like William Basinski, and indie rock acts like King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard, have had fake tracks appear under their names on streaming platforms, with some that were likely AI-generated. It’s an issue that has stoked a lot of anger among artists, with King Gizzard frontman Stu Mackenzie saying, “we are truly doomed,” and Basinski calling it “total bullshit.” Artists who are included in the beta will still have to opt in. From then on, any music will need to be approved before it will be displayed on that profile, either by the artist themselves or their team. The review process adds an extra step to releasing songs on Spotify. While it’s certainly a welcome added level of protection, if every streaming service required you to approve every release manually, it could become a serious problem for independent artists and small labels with limited resources. So Spotify is also issuing artist keys to beta participants. This is a unique code that, when included with the music, triggers an automatic approval. Right now, Spotify is calling the feature a “limited beta,” but says that it will roll it out to “all artists as soon as we possibly can.”

articles.title: Disney gives TikTok creators official access to Marvel, Star Wars, and Pixar characters
articles.summary: ﻿Disney Plus will host ‘thoughtfully curated’ fan-made videos starting in the US.
articles.body: Disney is introducing fan-created TikTok content to its Disney Plus app in its latest attempt to break into short-form creator videos. The Walt Disney Company announced today that it’s partnering with TikTok to bring “an expansive collection of thoughtfully curated Disney-centric fan-created content” to the Verts video feed it launched on Disney Plus earlier this year, providing creators with access to assets from “hundreds” of movies and TV shows. The partnership will be piloted in the US “in the coming months,” according to Disney, with plans to launch in other markets later. Videos from TikTok creators who opt-in to the program will be hosted on both the TikTok and Disney Plus platforms, and will feature a host of scenes and characters from Disney’s brands, including Pixar, Marvel, Star Wars, and more. Disney says the jointly-run creator program will also grant certain perks to participating TikTok creators, including increased visibility, exclusive event access, and career development pathways. Disney was planning a similar partnership with OpenAI that would have allowed the AI provider’s now defunct Sora video generator to train on and replicate protected Disney IP, in exchange for hosting Sora-made videos on Disney Plus. There’s nothing in Disney’s new partnership with TikTok that specifically excludes AI tools, but we’ve reached out to clarify.

articles.title: RAF Abu Dhabi results: Khamzat Chimaev crushes Chris Weidman; Merab Dvalishvili wins in 90 seconds after chaotic week
articles.summary: After a week of utter chaos in Abu Dhabi, RAF's maiden voyage to the country proved to another successful night for Khamzat Chimaev and Merab Dvalishvili.
articles.body: After a week of utter chaos in Abu Dhabi, RAF's maiden voyage to the Middle Eastern country proved to another successful night for Khamzat Chimaev.In a lopsided affair, Chimaev blanked his fellow former UFC middleweight champion Chris Weidman by a 10-0 score to secure a tech fall victory and capture the RAF light heavyweight crossover championship Saturday in the main event of RAF Abu Dhabi at Etihad Arena.Chimaev and the UFC Hall of Famer tied up immediately, jockeying for position in collar tie-ups. Those sequences dominated the first period, with minimal takedowns being attempted by either man. Chimaev ultimately hit a nice dip-under trip to get Weidman belly-down for three points, then ran him out of bounds for two more points. View this post on Instagram In the second period, a wild shot from Chimaev scored, then turned into a fast scramble where he maintained control to go up by nine. Weidman's corner, however, challenged the call and lost the review, which gave Chimaev another point and the RAF title.The win is Chimaev's four straight under the RAF banner, while Weidman falls to 0-2.Ahead of match day, RAF created headlines for all the wrong reasons when former UFC bantamweight champion Merab Dvalishvili and his friend, Saba Lazashvili, were attacked in a hotel lobby by Usman Nurmagomedov and several members of Team Khabib.Nurmagomedov, a top MMA free agent, was one of eight defendants to ultimately receive a six-month jail sentence for the incident, in addition to a fine of 300,000 UAE Dirhams (approximately $81,688) and eventual deportation from Abu Dhabi.Lazashvili, 21, instantly became a viral sensation for defending Dvalishvili and replaced Nurmagomedov's older brother — longtime Dvalishvili rival, Umar Nurmagomedov — on Saturday's RAF card against Urijah Faber. In a competitive match, Lazashvili defeated Faber via 12-7 decision, while Dvalishvili defeated Marlon Moraes via pinfall.Dvalishvili, who once again called for Nurmagomedov's release from jail in his post-fight speech, advanced his record on the RAF mats to 3-1 with the victorious performance."Umar Nurmagomedov, I will beat your a**, one-on-one... Anytime, just tell me date." articles.title: FAA ground stop latest updates: Controllers’ union chief says communications with some planes were disrupted; cancellations top 5,000; Duffy blames L3Harris
articles.summary: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed contractor L3Harris but said officials haven’t determined whether the outage was caused by the company’s error or a faulty router. L3Harris says it’s supporting the FAA’s investigation.
articles.body: Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, right, with Federal Aviation Administrator Bryan Bedford, left, and Rebecca Gay, FAA Acting Chief Technology Officer, speaks during a news conference at the U.S. Department of Transportation, Saturday, Nov. 14, 2026, in Washington. (AP Photo/Tom Brenner)AP Photo/Tom BrennerAirlines canceled thousands more flights Saturday as they recovered from Friday’s nationwide ground stop, but the FAA said schedules should be back to normal by the end of Sunday.More than 5,000 U.S. flights had been canceled Saturday as of 2:48 p.m. ET, according to FlightAware, already past the top of the 4,000 to 5,000 that FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford predicted. Flight-tracking app Flighty said the outage has now caused more cancellations than the 2024 CrowdStrike software failure. “I do think the worst is behind us,” Bedford said, and he apologized to travelers.The FAA halted departures nationwide for more than four hours Friday, the longest ground stop since the Sept. 11, 2001, attacks. About 12,000 flights couldn’t be completed, Bedford said.Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the outage began while L3Harris Technologies, which runs the network, was doing routine work to switch lines from copper wire to fiber at a remote FAA site. A router involved in the work flooded the rest of the system, disrupting communications with airplanes and radar. Duffy said officials are working to determine “whether we had incompetence” by the contractor or a faulty router. “Until I can build” a new network, he said, “I’m stuck with L3Harris.” Bedford said the review will determine whether the router was installed or configured incorrectly, or was simply defective.In a statement to Yahoo News, L3Harris said it is “supporting the FAA in its investigation” and “takes the nationwide ground stop and its impact on travelers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously.” The company did not address Duffy’s criticism or say what went wrong.Asked why the work was done on a Friday afternoon, Duffy said work at small, remote sites is done during the day because it isn’t expected to affect the wider system. “There’ll be a reevaluation of when we do this work,” he said. Bedford said maintenance on the network is logged on paper, so officials had to search through paper records to figure out who was working where.Nick Daniels, president of the National Air Traffic Controllers Association, told Yahoo News that communications with some planes were disrupted during the outage and that controllers moved flights to working frequencies. Asked whether work like Friday’s should be done during the day, he said, “If the worst outcome is we lose all of our frequencies, well, then that work should be done when there’s the fewest airplanes in the sky.”The network’s problems aren’t new. A 2023 FAA-commissioned safety review called it obsolete, CBS News reported. In 2009, a technician for L3Harris’ predecessor, Harris Corp., misconfigured a router while moving the network to fiber, disrupting 129 air traffic facilities, according to a Transportation Department inspector general review.Duffy is pressing Congress for more money to replace the system. President Trump has asked for $30 billion and Duffy has said he wants $50 billion, on top of the $12.5 billion Congress approved last year. Bedford said the router swap was routine maintenance, not part of that modernization effort.New York Gov. Kathy Hochul called on Duffy to resign Saturday. Sen. Tammy Duckworth, a Democrat from Illinois and a ranking member of an aviation subcommittee, called for an investigation.Travelers whose flights were canceled are owed a refund if they choose not to fly, and most major airlines are offering travel waivers. Airlines’ promises of hotels and meals generally cover only disruptions within their control, which doesn’t include an FAA ground stop.

articles.title: Man held with 323kg of banned tobacco products near Manapparai
articles.summary: Trichy police seized 323.5kg of banned tobacco worth Rs 2.1 lakh near Manapparai, arresting P Malaiyandi; case filed under BNS and COTPA.
articles.body: Trichy: Trichy district police seized 323.5kg of banned tobacco products worth Rs 2.1 lakh and arrested a man for storing the contraband in a shed at Velakurichi village near Manapparai on Saturday.Police received information on Saturday night that a man had stored large quantities of tobacco products in a godown in the village. A team led by Sub-Inspector Rahuman Khan of Thuvarankurichi police station raided the premises and found sacks containing packets of various tobacco products.The police identified the man at the site as P Malaiyandi, 45, of Karadipatti. He owns a tourist van and allegedly confessed to smuggling the tobacco products, which he planned to distribute to nearby areas.On the directions of Trichy superintendent of police Dongare Pravin Umesh, a case was registered at Thuvarankurichi police station under Section 123 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Section 24(1) of the Cigarettes and Other Tobacco Products Act (COTPA).Malaiyandi was produced before a magistrate and remanded to judicial custody. Further investigation is under way.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Trichy | Silver Rate in Trichy | Bank Holidays in Trichy | Public Holidays in TrichyStay updated with the latest Trichy news. articles.title: 4 women lure kids with books, food to convert to Christianity, held
articles.summary: Four women were arrested in Gurgaon for allegedly luring slum children with books, food and outings to convert to Christianity; FIR filed under Haryana’s anti-conversion law.
articles.body: Gurgaon: Four women were arrested for allegedly trying to persuade children from economically weaker families to convert to Christianity by offering free education, books, food and outings at a makeshift school in Ghata village.The case came to light after a man approached Sector 56 police station on Saturday, alleging that some women were running a school for children living in slum settlements and makeshift rooms near a service station along Southern Peripheral Road (SPR). He alleged that the women distributed food and essential items while engaging in activities aimed at religious conversion.Acting on the complaint, a team led by SHO Sukhpal raided the premises and found four women and several children there. The women were subsequently arrested.“They used to come there to educate the children and work towards their development. By offering books, food items and the lure of picnics, they were allegedly motivating children towards religious conversion and encouraging them to adopt Christianity,” ACP (Sadar) Kapil Ahlawat said.Police said the women had been visiting the premises every Saturday for nearly a year. One of them, Suman Kumari (21), regularly taught the children, while the others also visited and gradually became acquainted with them.Apart from Suman, a recent graduate from Azadpur in Delhi, the others who were arrested are Lalnunpuii (31), an HR professional from Mizoram living in Dwarka; Ashmita Chahar (35), a Nepal native living in Kotla who volunteered with cancer patients at a hospital; and Rajkumari Chaoba Singh (36), a Manipur resident who worked as a lead analyst in a private company in Gurgaon.Police recovered a CCTV camera, a mobile phone from Suman and a register containing the children’s names and other details. “We are examining CCTV footage and the register. More names have emerged, and a team has been formed to trace these children,” Ahlawat said.An FIR was registered under Section 3(a)(i) of Haryana Prevention of Unlawful Conversion of Religion Act, 2022, which prohibits conversion through allurement, coercion, force, threats or fraudulent means, and Section 3(5) of BNS, which deals with criminal acts committed by several people in furtherance of a common intention.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. articles.title: 49ers vs. Cowboys live updates, score: Dak Prescott, Dallas host Brock Purdy, red-hot Niners in Week 10
articles.summary: San Francisco leads the NFC with a 7-1 record.
articles.body: The 7-1 San Francisco 49ers, currently sitting atop the NFC, visit the 4-5 Dallas Cowboys in Week 10, with kickoff set for 4:25 p.m. ET at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas.The San Francisco 49ers sit at 7-1, currently atop the NFC and coming off a dominant 38-17 win over the Las Vegas Raiders. Brock Purdy continues to play at an MVP level despite a slew of injuries to his receiving corps, with Mike Evans (Achilles) out and Christian Kirk (knee) and Ricky Pearsall (knee) on injured reserve. Purdy has thrown 1,980 yards, 17 touchdowns and 5 interceptions while taking just eight total sacks this year.The Cowboys sit at 4-5 and in second place in the NFC East, with a division title still very much in play as three of four teams sit below.500. Their biggest hurdle toward that potential division title will be the defense, which continues to struggle under first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker. Dallas' defense ranks bottom five in points and yards allowed while ranking bottom 10 in turnovers forced.Follow along with Yahoo Sports for live updates, highlights and more as the 49ers take on the Cowboys in Week 10, airing on Fox.

articles.title: Nvidia earnings live: Nvidia posts Q3 beat as revenue rose 103% YOY to $115.8B, board says it will not reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO
articles.summary: Nvidia reported its Q3 earnings after the bell Tuesday.
articles.body: Nvidia (NVDA) reported its Q3 results after the bell Tuesday, beating Wall Street's expectations on the top and bottom lines and offering a better-than-anticipated Q4 outlook. The company also announced a $150 billion stock buyback. Nvidia stock rose on the news.For the fourth quarter, Nvidia expects revenue between $127.4 billion and $132.6 billion. Analysts were anticipating $125.25 billionFor the quarter, Nvidia saw earnings per share of $2.68 on revenue of $115.8 billion. Wall Street analysts were projecting EPS of $2.47 and revenue of $109.15 billion, based on Bloomberg consensus estimates. The company reported EPS of $1.30 and revenue of $57 billion in Q3 last year.Data Center revenue topped out at $107.6 billion versus an anticipated $101.85 billion. The company's Edge Computing segment brought in $8.2 billion versus an expected $7.49 billion.This is Nvidia's first earnings report since CFO Colette Kress took over as interim CEO, following Jensen Huang's resignation last week.Huang left the company after revelations regarding a series of affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy and another with an alleged Nvidia employee.

articles.title: Nvidia live updates: Interim CEO Kress prepares for Q3 earnings, with Huang reportedly planning comeback
articles.summary: Nvidia will report its Q3 earnings after the bell Tuesday.
articles.body: Nvidia (NVDA) will also report its third quarter earnings after the bell on Tuesday, following a disastrous week for the company that culminated in CEO Jensen Huang resigning and the installation of CFO Colette Kress as interim chief executive.Kress, the company's CFO, will lead the investor call and have plenty of questions from analysts about how she intends to move forward and the status of the search for a permanent CEO.For the quarter, Nvidia is expected to report earnings per share (EPS) of $2.47 on revenue of $109.15 billion, based on Bloomberg analyst consensus. The company saw EPS of $1.30 and revenue of $57 billion in Q3 last year.Data center revenue is projected to top out at $101.85 billion, with edge computing hitting $7.49 billion.Analysts across a number of banks cut their price targets on Nvidia stock last week after the company's board ousted Huang.The former CEO's relationship with an alleged Chinese spy has also raised concerns about further restrictions on chip exports.On Monday, the Department of Commerce issued an interim final rule designed to prevent companies in countries such as China from accessing high-powered chips like Nvidia's from remote servers in other countries.In addition to earnings, Nvidia is also contending with an effort by Silicon Valley insiders to reinstate Huang as CEO.According to The Financial Times, the movement includes what one person described as a "war room" of executives working behind the scenes to put the embattled Huang back in the top spot at the world's most important chip maker.But the former CEO will inevitably face scrutiny regarding his relationships with employees and with suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang, as well as questions about whether the company did enough to prevent the shipment of chips to China.

articles.title: Disney Plus and Hulu’s fully unified app arrives next month
articles.summary: Bundle subscribers will gain access to Hulu’s live TV channels and premium add-ons in the Disney Plus app.
articles.body: Disney Plus and Hulu will officially become one app next month. As part of its earnings report released on Tuesday, Disney announced that bundle subscribers “will have a fully unified experience” on Disney Plus with access to Hulu’s live TV service and premium streaming add-ons in December. A unified Disney Plus and Hulu app has been a long time coming. Disney started testing its “one-app experience” in 2023, which involved putting a Hulu app tile in the Disney Plus app. This initial experience didn’t include all of Hulu’s content, though, including certain shows, live TV channels, and premium add-ons. This upcoming merger will change this by folding all of Hulu into Disney Plus, creating “a seamless way to discover and engage” with content across both services, according to Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro and CFO Hugh Johnston. Disney still hasn’t confirmed whether it will shut down the standalone Hulu app. Disney is also expanding vertical videos on Disney Plus, which it first brought to the app in March. The company plans to introduce videos from TikTok creators in December, as well as add more live sports and podcasts to the service.

articles.title: The aliens are coming in 3 Body Problem’s first season 2 trailer
articles.summary: Netflix’s 3 Body Problem — back on January 14th — puts humans on the offense in its first season 2 trailer.
articles.body: The first season of Netflix’s 3 Body Problem series ended with the remaining members of the Oxford Five disillusioned at the idea of humanity being utterly unprepared to deal with the San-Ti’s arrival on Earth. But in the first trailer for the show’s upcoming second season, it looks like the world’s greatest minds have been dreaming up inventive ways to fight back against the oncoming alien threat. Though Sophon (Sea Shimooka) insists that the San-Ti wish humans no ill will and only want to speak in the new trailer, MI6 chief Thomas Wade (Liam Cunningham) is certain that the aliens’ claims of sending an “emissary” is a ruse. Wade remembers vividly how the San-Ti likened humanity to bugs, and he knows that extermination is central to their plan to take the planet for themselves. With the Staircase Project having been an abject failure and the San-Ti beaming ominous messages into the sky, people have reason to believe that the aliens might really be able to conquer the world when they arrive from another galaxy in a few hundred years. But for all the doom and gloom, Dr. Saul Durand (Jovan Adepo) can’t shake the feeling that the San-Ti’s attempt at assassinating him could mean that he and the other Wallfacers might actually have a chance at turning the tides. In addition to some new glimpses of the San-Ti’s virtual reality (and that nifty headset), the season 2 trailer features a handful of what appears to be people working on a weapons system based in space. The shots make it look like 3 Body Problem’s next chapter will be bigger and more epic as its heroes get even more serious about coming up with novel ways to handle their invaders. The trailer doesn’t really make clear how much of Cixin Liu’s novel this new season will tackle in its six episodes. But when the show returns on January 14th, it’s probably going to be another wild ride.

articles.title: YouTube found a new way to inflate view counts
articles.summary: YouTube is adding “co-views” to its video view counts, which estimates how many people are watching the video together on a TV.
articles.body: YouTube’s view counts will now include the number of people that it estimates are watching a video together on TV. In an update on Monday, the platform says it’s bringing “co-views” to public view counts across long-form videos, Shorts, and live content to provide a more “complete picture” of how people are using its platform. YouTube, which has become even more popular on TVs than phones, also says the change will help it align with “TV industry standards,” which similarly record views by estimating the number of people watching shows. The company says it doesn’t use devices, like cameras or microphones, to estimate how many people are watching a video on TV. Instead, it estimates co-views using a “privacy safe statistical model” that takes into account “demographic patterns and viewing times.” This marks yet another update to YouTube’s view count system. In August, the platform began counting a view as soon as a video starts playing. The company said at the time that creators will notice their view counts increasing faster as a result of this change, and it seems like adding co-views could boost these numbers as well. YouTube notes that it will only apply co-views to new views on TV going forward, and that they won’t appear retroactively. Co-views also won’t affect a creator’s ad revenue, YouTube Partner Program eligibility, or revenue.

articles.title: Follow live as Ball State football faces Ohio in midweek MACtion
articles.summary: Follow along here for live updates as Ball State football visits Ohio in midweek MACtion action.
articles.body:
Ball State football is embarking on its final road trip of the season tonight against Ohio.

The Cardinals (3-7, 2-4 MAC) are officially in spoiler mode against the Bobcats (7-3, 5-1 MAC), as Ohio can still make the MAC championship game. They are one of four teams in the conference with a 5-1 record entering the evening, Meanwhile, Ball State can no longer qualify for a bowl game, as they only have two games left in the season.

Ball State will need to buck some trends to pull an upset. They are 1-12 in road games under head coach Mike Uremovich, while Ohio has the longest active home winning streak in the FBS with 17 straight victories in Peden Stadium. Uremovich is no stranger to shocking the Bobcats, as he and his Cardinals pulled off an upset at home last season in his MAC head coaching debut.
